decisions.quote: Since the value of t statistic is not precisely the same as in the article, the resulted outcome is “did not reproduce”. The difference is however only very subtle, probably due to the different statistical software used by original authors. I want to add that mean in enjoyability of the program for commercial group was 5.377358 and for no commercial group was 4.469388 which coincides with means provided in the article (5.38 vs 4.47).
decisions.location: Claim evaluations, Claim ID: single-trace, Discussion (line 67); see also Analysis attempt 1 (line 10) and Claim ID: gpp38z (lines 113-114)
decisions.reason: Re-running the analysis on the original Study 2 dataset reproduced the exact sample size (N = 102), group means, and p-values across both tested claims (Claim gpp38z matched t = 2.00 and p = 0.048 after rounding; Claim single-trace matched M = 5.38 vs. 4.47 and p = 0.016, with t = 2.4466 vs. reported t = 2.43). Although the strict SCORE 'Precise Reproduction Criteria' triggered a 'did not reproduce' label on Claim single-trace for the 0.0166 difference in the t-statistic, the analyst explicitly notes in the overview that 'This first attempt produced the same results as provided in the article' and explains that the t-statistic difference is 'only very subtle, probably due to the different statistical software used by original authors.' Under the codebook, rounding and negligible numerical differences that are not treated as substantive discrepancies are coded as 'computationally reproducible'.
